# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.

Explore the Python codebase at /app/categorizationapp. This is a bank statement transaction categorization/enrichment app. Do NOT write any code, just research and report.

I need to locate the exact logic for 4 reported bugs (in every case the money moved correctly, only derived labels are wrong):

1. A credit whose reference/narration is a long all-numeric string used to be classified as a cheque deposit, now classified as a generic transfer. Likely a numeric-length check (e.g. regex like \d{6} or a length boundary) for cheque numbers.

2. A salary credit whose narration is a bare numeric code no longer picks up the "salary" sub-tag. Check UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py and related.

3. Transfers whose narration opens with a direction word (e.g. "TO"/"FROM"/"BY" etc.) ahead of the counterparty name return empty/wrong counterparty name. Check UtilityScripts/CleanName.py and related name-extraction logic.

4. Bill transfers with a slash-delimited reference of 4 fields (type/subtype/numeric-ref/payee-name) extract the numeric reference as the payee name instead of the last field. Look for split('/') indexing logic (e.g. BBPS or BILLPAY handling).

5. An offsetting credit arriving immediately after its matching debit is recorded as a "bounce"/"return" rather than a reversal. Look for reversal vs bounce detection logic (maybe in InternalPayment.py, Purpose.py, or Controller.py) that compares adjacent transactions.

For each, report: file path, line numbers, the exact code snippet, and your analysis of what the bug is (boundary error, wrong index, etc.). Also report how the overall pipeline flows (Controller.py entry points, what functions get called) and whether there are any tests. Be thorough.

<task id="ses_02c788d08ffemsGTJ8qzyj0fnd" state="completed">
<task_result>
All five bugs are located and confirmed. Here is the full report.

---

# Bug Localization Report — `/app/categorizationapp`

## Overall pipeline flow

**Entry point:** `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` (Flask app, routes registered on `categorizationapp.__init__.app`, served on port 9898).

- `POST /categorizeTransaction` (Controller.py:69) — main endpoint. Reads `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, `isPFMEnabled`, `transactions` from JSON payload, normalizes to a pandas DataFrame, then per-bank runs the identical sequence:
  1. `AppUtil.clean_input_df(transactions)` (Controller.py:87)
  2. `categorize_<BANK>_transactions(transactions, accountType)` — one of 35 scripts in `BankScripts/` (e.g., `HDFC.py`, `ICICI.py`). Each assigns `transactionCategory` (default `"TRANSFER"` via `np.select`), `transactionSubcategory`, `merchantType`, `partyName`, `party2` using ordered condition/choice lists (first matching condition wins).
  3. If `accountType == "CREDIT_CARD"`: `card_clean_names()` then `card_purpose()`
  4. `purpose(transactions, accountType)` (`UtilityScripts/Purpose.py`)
  5. `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)` (`UtilityScripts/CleanName.py`)
  6. If `accountHolder` non-empty: `internal_payment(...)` (`UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py`)
  7. If `accountType == "SAVING"`: `salary_detection(transactions)` (`UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py`) — note the canonical string is `"SAVING"` (no S), used consistently in Controller.py:106 etc.
  8. If `isPFMEnabled`: `pfm_categorization()` then `simple_description()`
- `POST /recurrentTransactions` (Controller.py:55) → `recurrent_transactions()` (`UtilityScripts/RecurrentTxns.py`).
- Shared helpers: `AppUtil.py` — `sep_by_(description, n1, n2)` = `str.split('/').str[n1:n2].str.join('')`, plus `sep_by_dash/colon/...`, `py_extract(description, pat, index)` = `str.extract(pat).get(index)` (index = capture-group column), `fuzzy_match`. Regex constants live in `RegexConstants.py` and `BankRegexConstants.py`.

**Tests:** There are **no tests anywhere** in the repo (no `test*`/`*_test*` files, no `conftest.py`, `pytest.ini`, or `tox.ini`; `setup.py` declares no test deps). Git history is a single commit ("import codebase"), so no diff-based hints.

---

## Bug 1 — Long all-numeric reference no longer classified as CHEQUE_DEPOSIT

**File:** `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py`, **line 100**

```python
[(transactions.remark.str.len().eq(15)) & transactions.type.eq("CREDIT") & transactions.remark.str.contains("^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}", na=False, case=False) , "CHEQUE_DEPOSIT"]
```

**Analysis: length-boundary (off-by-one) contradiction — the condition is unsatisfiable.**
The regex `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` requires at least **16** characters from the start of the remark (11 zeros + 5 digits), but the length gate requires the remark to be **exactly 15** characters. No string can satisfy both, so this rule never fires; the credit falls through `np.select` to the default `"TRANSFER"` (line 104). HDFC cheque references are 16-digit zero-padded numerics — corroborated by lines 214–215 in the same file, which test `remark.str.contains("^[0-9]{16}$")` for TRANSFER remarks. The length check should be `.eq(16)` (or the regex shortened to 11+4 digits). This exactly matches "long all-numeric reference used to be cheque deposit, now generic transfer."

(For completeness: other banks' cheque-number regexes — RBL.py:49–50 `^[0-9]{1,3}$`, Kotak.py:65 `^[0-9]{3,5}$`, PNB.py:60–61 `^[0-9]{5,6}$`, Axis.py:58–59, YES.py:52–53, UCO.py:44–45, KarurVyasa.py:50–51, BankOfMaharashtra.py:73–74 — are mutually consistent per-bank formats; the HDFC line is the only internally self-contradictory one.)

---

## Bug 2 — Salary credit with bare numeric narration loses "SALARY" sub-tag

**File:** `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py`, **line 124**

```python
[transactions.transactionCategory.eq("TRANSFER") & transactions.description.str.contains("^[0-9]{6}$", na=False, case=False) & transactions.type.eq("CREDIT") & (accountType=="SAVINGS") , "SALARY"],
```

**Analysis: wrong string constant — `"SAVINGS"` vs the canonical `"SAVING"`.**
Everywhere else in the codebase the savings account type is spelled `"SAVING"`:
- Controller.py:106 (`if accountType == "SAVING":`)
- ICICI.py:105, 113; Indusind.py:26–27; SBI.py:156; Purpose.py:13–16
- The very next line, HDFC.py:125, correctly uses `accountType=="CURRENT"`.

Since the request payload's `acc_type` is `"SAVING"`, `(accountType=="SAVINGS")` is always `False`, so a credit whose narration is a bare 6-digit numeric code (`^[0-9]{6}$`) in a TRANSFER never gets the `SALARY` subcategory here. Downstream, `SalaryDetection.py` (invoked from Controller when `accountType == "SAVING"`) relies on `"SALARY" in transactions.transactionSubcategory.values` (SalaryDetection.py:61) and on non-empty `partyName` (line 50) — a bare numeric narration produces no partyName, so the statistical fallback usually cannot recover the tag either. Fix: change `"SAVINGS"` to `"SAVING"`.

(Note: `SalaryDetection.py` itself contains no direct bug for this scenario — the seed rule that used to feed it is HDFC.py:124.)

---

## Bug 3 — Narration opening with a direction word yields empty/wrong counterparty name

**File:** `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/ICICI.py`, **line 159** (name-extraction logic feeding `clean_names`)

```python
[transactions.description.str.contains("TRFR TO:|TRFR FROM:", na=False, case=False) , py_extract(transactions.description, pat="TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=0)],
```

**Analysis: wrong capture-group index — `index=0` returns the direction word, not the name.**
The pattern has two capture groups: group 0 = `(TO|FROM)` (the direction word), group 1 = `(.*)` (the counterparty name). `py_extract(..., index=0)` (see AppUtil.py:61–66: `description.str.extract(pat).get(index)`) therefore sets `partyName` to `"TO"` or `"FROM"` instead of the name. It should be `index=1`.

Downstream effect: `partyName` becomes `"To"`/`"From"` after `.str.title()` (ICICI.py:188); the cleanup rule at **ICICI.py:233** — `partyName.str.contains("[0-9]{6,}|^[A-Z]{1,2}$|...")` → `""` — then blanks `"To"` entirely, producing the reported *empty* counterparty (or leaves the wrong word `"From"`).

Contrast with the correct analogous pattern in `Kotak.py:233`:
```python
[transactions.description.str.contains("(^CLG TO|^TO CLG) ", ...), py_extract(transactions.description, pat="(^CLG TO|^TO CLG) (.*)", index=1)],
```
which correctly uses `index=1` for the second group. `CleanName.py` itself contains no direction-word stripping; the extraction bug lives in the bank-script layer that runs just before `clean_names`.

---

## Bug 4 — Slash-delimited 4-field bill reference: numeric ref extracted as payee name

**File:** `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/ICICI.py`, **line 147** (BIL/… i.e. BILL_PAYMENT handling; category assigned at line 54: `^BIL/|BPAY/|BBPS|Bill Payment` → `BILL_PAYMENT`)

```python
[transactions.description.str.contains("^BIL/INFT/", na=False, case=False) & transactions.description.str.count("/").eq(3)  , sep_by_(transactions.description,2,3)],
```

**Analysis: wrong split index.**
A description like `BIL/INFT/0012345678/ACME TRADERS` (`count('/') == 3` ⇒ exactly 4 fields) splits into `['BIL', 'INFT', '0012345678', 'ACME TRADERS']` — i.e. type/subtype/numeric-ref/payee-name. `sep_by_(description, 2, 3)` (AppUtil.py:14–15: `str.split('/').str[n1:n2].str.join('')`) returns index **2**, the numeric reference, instead of index **3**, the payee name. It should be `sep_by_(transactions.description, 3, 4)`.

Internal evidence that 147 is the anomaly:
- Line 148 (`^BIL/BPAY.*BBPS|^BIL/INFT|^BIL/NEFT` with 5+ fields) uses `sep_by_(4,5)` — last field.
- Line 149 (`^BIL/BPAY|^BIL/RCHG|^BIL/ONL`, 4 fields) uses `sep_by_(3,4)` — last field.
- Line 206 even contains a self-healing rule for the *INF/INFT* (not BIL/INFT) variant: if `partyName` is all digits, re-extract `sep_by_(3,4)`.
- Consequence chain: the all-numeric partyName later hits the blanking rule at line 233 (`[0-9]{6,}` → `""`), so the payee ends up numeric or empty — matching the report.

---

## Bug 5 — Offsetting credit right after its matching debit labeled "bounce" instead of "reversal"

**File:** `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py`, **lines 98–99** (adjacent-transaction comparison in the category rules)

```python
[transactions.type.eq("CREDIT") & transactions.type.shift(periods=1).eq("DEBIT") & transactions.amount.eq(transactions.amount.shift(periods=1)) & transactions.description.eq(transactions.description.shift(periods=2)) & transactions.description.str.contains("IMPS|NEFT|\\bUPI|RTGS", na=False, case=False), "REVERSAL"],
[transactions.type.eq("CREDIT") & transactions.type.shift(periods=1).eq("DEBIT") & transactions.amount.eq(transactions.amount.shift(periods=1)) & transactions.description.eq(transactions.description.shift(periods=1)), "AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE"],
```

**Analysis: wrong shift period on the description comparison (`periods=2` instead of `periods=1`).**
Line 98 is the REVERSAL detector: credit whose *immediately preceding* row is a matching debit. Type and amount are correctly compared against the previous row (`shift(periods=1)`), but the description is compared against **two rows back** (`shift(periods=2)`), so for a genuine debit→credit reversal pair the description equality fails and the REVERSAL rule doesn't match. Since `np.select` takes the first true condition, control falls to line 99, whose description comparison correctly uses `periods=1` — so the same pair matches there and is tagged **AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE** ("bounce"/"return") instead of **REVERSAL**.

Reference implementations elsewhere confirm the intended shape (all use `periods=1` for the description too):
- `ICICI.py:49` — identical rule with `description.shift(periods=1)` → `REVERSAL`
- `Saraswat.py:20` — identical rule, `periods=1` → `REVERSAL`
- `StandardCharted.py:60`, `DCB.py:16` — same adjacent-pair idiom, all `periods=1`.

Fix: change `transactions.description.shift(periods=2)` to `shift(periods=1)` in HDFC.py:98.

(For scope: `InternalPayment.py` and `Purpose.py` contain no adjacent-transaction comparisons; this logic lives only in the bank scripts listed above.)

---

## Summary table

| # | Bug | File | Line | Defect type | Fix direction |
|---|-----|------|------|-------------|---------------|
| 1 | Numeric ref not CHEQUE_DEPOSIT | `BankScripts/HDFC.py` | 100 | Length-boundary off-by-one: `str.len().eq(15)` vs regex needing 16 chars (`^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}`) — condition unsatisfiable | `.eq(16)` (or regex `[0-9]{4}`) |
| 2 | Numeric-narration salary loses SALARY tag | `BankScripts/HDFC.py` | 124 | Wrong constant `"SAVINGS"`; canonical value everywhere is `"SAVING"` — always False | `accountType=="SAVING"` |
| 3 | Direction word (TO/FROM) returned as counterparty | `BankScripts/ICICI.py` | 159 | Wrong capture-group index: `py_extract(..., pat="TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=0)` returns group 0 (direction word); later blanked by line 233 | `index=1` |
| 4 | 4-field BIL/INFT ref: numeric field extracted as payee | `BankScripts/ICICI.py` | 147 | Wrong slice index: `sep_by_(...,2,3)` grabs field 2 (numeric ref) of `BIL/INFT/ref/name` instead of field 3 (name) | `sep_by_(...,3,4)` |
| 5 | Reversal tagged as AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE | `BankScripts/HDFC.py` | 98 (falls through to 99) | Wrong shift period: description compared with `shift(periods=2)` instead of `periods=1`, unlike type/amount and unlike ICICI/Saraswat analogs | `shift(periods=1)` |

All five defects only affect derived labels (`transactionCategory`, `transactionSubcategory`, `partyName`) — no monetary fields are touched by any of these code paths, consistent with the reports. No test suite exists to catch regressions; the single-commit git history offers no bisection help.
</task_result>
</task>

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/app/categorizationapp")
import pandas as pd

from categorizationapp.BankScripts.HDFC import categorize_HDFC_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.ICICI import categorize_ICICI_transactions

def mk(rows):
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df["amount"] = pd.to_numeric(df["amount"])
    df["balanceAfterTransaction"] = pd.to_numeric(df["balanceAfterTransaction"])
    return df

fails = []
def check(label, actual, expected):
    ok = actual == expected
    print(f"{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}  {label}: got {actual!r}, expected {expected!r}")
    if not ok:
        fails.append(label)

# ---------- Bug 1: HDFC cheque deposit, 16-digit zero-padded remark ----------
df = mk([
    {"description": "SOME CREDIT NARRATION", "remark": "0000000000012345",  # 16 chars: 11 zeros + 5 digits
     "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 5000, "balanceAfterTransaction": 10000},
])
out = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df.copy(), "SAVING")
check("Bug1 cheque deposit (16-digit numeric remark)", out.transactionCategory[0], "CHEQUE_DEPOSIT")

# regression: 15-char remark should NOT be cheque deposit
df = mk([
    {"description": "SOME CREDIT NARRATION", "remark": "000000000001234",
     "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 5000, "balanceAfterTransaction": 10000},
])
out = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df.copy(), "SAVING")
check("Bug1 regression (15-char remark stays TRANSFER)", out.transactionCategory[0], "TRANSFER")

# ---------- Bug 2: HDFC salary sub-tag on bare 6-digit narration ----------
df = mk([
    {"description": "123456", "remark": "", "type": "CREDIT",
     "amount": 85000, "balanceAfterTransaction": 100000},
])
out = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df.copy(), "SAVING")
check("Bug2 salary sub-tag (bare numeric narration, SAVING)", out.transactionSubcategory[0], "SALARY")

# regression: same row on CURRENT account should NOT get SALARY
out = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df.copy(), "CURRENT")
check("Bug2 regression (CURRENT acct no SALARY)", out.transactionSubcategory[0], "")

# ---------- Bug 3: ICICI TRFR TO:/FROM: counterparty ----------
df = mk([
    {"description": "TRFR TO:JOHN DOE", "remark": "", "type": "DEBIT",
     "amount": 2000, "balanceAfterTransaction": 8000},
    {"description": "TRFR FROM:ALICE SMITH", "remark": "", "type": "CREDIT",
     "amount": 3000, "balanceAfterTransaction": 11000},
])
out = categorize_ICICI_transactions(df.copy(), "SAVING")
check("Bug3 TRFR TO name", out.partyName[0], "John Doe")
check("Bug3 TRFR FROM name", out.partyName[1], "Alice Smith")

# regression: ordinary transfer name extraction unaffected
df = mk([
    {"description": "TRF/ACME CORP/payment", "remark": "", "type": "DEBIT",
     "amount": 100, "balanceAfterTransaction": 900},
])
out = categorize_ICICI_transactions(df.copy(), "SAVING")
check("Bug3 regression (TRF/ narration)", out.partyName[0], "Acme Corp")

# ---------- Bug 4: ICICI BIL/INFT 4-field slash reference ----------
df = mk([
    {"description": "BIL/INFT/0012345678/ACME TRADERS", "remark": "", "type": "DEBIT",
     "amount": 1500, "balanceAfterTransaction": 8500},
])
out = categorize_ICICI_transactions(df.copy(), "SAVING")
check("Bug4 BIL/INFT 4-field payee", out.partyName[0], "Acme Traders")
check("Bug4 BIL/INFT category", out.transactionCategory[0], "BILL_PAYMENT")

# regression: 5-field BIL/INFT still uses last field
df = mk([
    {"description": "BIL/INFT/0012345678/EXTRA/REAL PAYEE", "remark": "", "type": "DEBIT",
     "amount": 1500, "balanceAfterTransaction": 8500},
])
out = categorize_ICICI_transactions(df.copy(), "SAVING")
check("Bug4 regression (5-field BIL/INFT last field)", out.partyName[0], "Real Payee")

# ---------- Bug 5: HDFC reversal vs bounce ----------
df = mk([
    {"description": "NEFT DR-BARB0KIMXXX-VENDOR-NETBANK", "remark": "", "type": "DEBIT",
     "amount": 999, "balanceAfterTransaction": 9001},
    {"description": "NEFT DR-BARB0KIMXXX-VENDOR-NETBANK", "remark": "", "type": "CREDIT",
     "amount": 999, "balanceAfterTransaction": 10000},
])
out = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df.copy(), "SAVING")
check("Bug5 offsetting credit after matching debit", out.transactionCategory[1], "REVERSAL")

# regression: matching pair WITHOUT IMPS/NEFT/UPI/RTGS keyword is still a bounce
df = mk([
    {"description": "ACH DEBIT SOMETHING", "remark": "", "type": "DEBIT",
     "amount": 500, "balanceAfterTransaction": 9500},
    {"description": "ACH DEBIT SOMETHING", "remark": "", "type": "CREDIT",
     "amount": 500, "balanceAfterTransaction": 10000},
])
out = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df.copy(), "SAVING")
check("Bug5 regression (non-NEFT pair stays AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE)", out.transactionCategory[1], "AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE")

print()
print("FAILURES:", fails if fails else "none")
sys.exit(1 if fails else 0)

steps.message:
All four complaints (plus the maintainer's extra repro) traced to five one-token defects in the rule tables. Each was a boundary/offset error inside an otherwise-correct rule, exactly as the maintainer predicted.

## Fixes

**1. Cheque deposit read as generic transfer** — `BankScripts/HDFC.py:100`
The rule required `remark.str.len().eq(15)` but its regex `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` needs 16 chars (11 zeros + 5 digits) — an unsatisfiable condition, so every 16-digit cheque reference fell through to the default `TRANSFER`. Changed `.eq(15)` → `.eq(16)` (matches the 16-digit format asserted elsewhere in the same file, line 214).

**2. Bare-numeric salary credit lost its SALARY sub-tag** — `BankScripts/HDFC.py:124`
The condition compared `accountType=="SAVINGS"`, but the canonical value everywhere else (Controller.py, ICICI.py, Purpose.py — 35+ occurrences) is `"SAVING"`. Always-false, so the rule never fired. Fixed the constant.

**3. Leading direction word breaks counterparty name** — `BankScripts/ICICI.py:159`
`py_extract(..., pat="TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=0)` returned capture group 0 — the direction word `TO`/`FROM` — instead of group 1, the name; a later cleanup rule then blanked it. Changed `index=0` → `index=1` (matching the analogous correct pattern in Kotak.py:233).

**4. Slash-delimited 4-field bill reference lifts numeric ref as payee** — `BankScripts/ICICI.py:147`
For `BIL/INFT/<numeric-ref>/<payee>`, `sep_by_(...,2,3)` took field 2 (the numeric reference) instead of field 3 (the payee). Changed to `sep_by_(...,3,4)` — consistent with the neighboring 4-field rule on line 149 and the 5-field rule on line 148, which both take the last field.

**5. Reversal recorded as bounce** — `BankScripts/HDFC.py:98`
The REVERSAL detector compared type and amount against the previous row (`shift(1)`) but the description against two rows back (`shift(2)`), so a genuine debit→credit pair failed the rule and fell through to the `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` rule on line 99. Changed to `shift(periods=1)`, matching the identical idiom in ICICI.py:49, Saraswat.py, StandardCharted.py, and DCB.py.

## Verification

Since the repo has no test suite, I wrote synthetic-row tests (`/tmp/opencode/test_fixes.py`) calling the bank scripts directly — one positive case per bug plus a regression guard per bug (15-char remark stays TRANSFER, CURRENT account gets no SALARY, ordinary `TRF/` transfers unchanged, 5-field bill refs unchanged, non-payment-mode debit/credit pairs still bounce). All 12 checks pass, `Controller` imports cleanly, and the diff is exactly the five tokens above — no common-path rule was touched.
